blocks.text: Ab teesra aur is hisse ka aakhri function: tangent. Yahan do nai baatein milengi. Pehli, tangent ka graph toota hua hai (asymptotes ki wajah se), is liye interval band (closed) nahin, khula (open) hoga. Doosri, \(\tan^{-1}\) har real number ko qabool karta hai, sirf \(-1\) se \(1\) tak nahin. Aur sabaq ke aakhir mein kitab ki pehli misaal (Example 1) hai, jis mein teeno inverse functions ki principal values nikalni hain.

Kitab kehti hai: function \(f(x) = \tan x\) ko dekhiye jis ka domain set \(\left\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R} \wedge x \ne (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\right\}\) hai aur range tamam real numbers ka set hai. Tangent ka graph Figure 9.7 mein hai. (Symbol \(\wedge\) ka matlab "aur" hai.)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "Consider the function define by \(f(x) = \tan x\) with domain is the set ..." chhapa hai. Sahi angrezi: "Consider the function defined by \(f(x) = \tan x\), with domain the set ...". Sirf grammar ki ghalti hai; domain aur range bilkul sahi hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke odd multiples domain se kyun nikale gaye? Kyun ke \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), aur \(\cos x = 0\) theek \(x = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}, \pm\frac{3\pi}{2}, \dots\) par hota hai, yani \(x = (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) par. Zero se divide karna mumkin nahin, is liye yeh points domain mein nahin.
Graph par yeh points dashed vertical lines ki shakal mein nazar aate hain. Inhein asymptote kehte hain (woh line jis ke qareeb graph jata hai magar chhoota nahi). Misaal: aap kisi deewar ki taraf har qadam pichle qadam ka aadha uthayein, to deewar ke qareeb se qareeb hote jayenge magar kabhi pahunchenge nahin.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = tan x from minus 3 pi over 2 to 3 pi over 2: three rising branches separated by dashed vertical asymptotes at x = minus 3 pi over 2, minus pi over 2, pi over 2 and 3 pi over 2. A dashed horizontal line y = 2 cuts every branch once.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.7: Graph of f(x) = tan x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Figure 9.7 ko ghor se dekhiye. Sine aur cosine ke graphs lehron (waves) jaise the jo \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan qaid the. Tangent ka graph bilkul alag hai: yeh kai alag alag tukron (branches) mein bata hua hai, har tukra neeche se bohat door (\(-\infty\) ki taraf) se shuru ho kar upar bohat door (\(+\infty\) ki taraf) tak jata hai, aur do tukron ke darmiyan ek dashed asymptote hai.
Har tukra lagataar barh raha hai, aur har tukre ki chaurai \(\pi\) hai, kyun ke tangent ka period \(\pi\) hai (sine aur cosine ka period \(2\pi\) tha). Isi liye har tukra bilkul pichle tukre ki naqal hai, bas \(\pi\) aage khiska hua.
Ab line \(y = 2\) dekhiye: yeh har tukre ko ek baar kaat ti hai, yani poore graph ko laatadaad baar. Horizontal line test fail! Isi liye poore domain par tangent one-to-one nahin. Lekin agar sirf ek tukra le lein, to har horizontal line use sirf ek baar kaategi. Yahi agla qadam hai.

Kitab kehti hai: saaf zahir hai ke tangent function bijective nahin, kyun ke line \(y = 2\) graph ko kai jagah kaat ti hai. Lekin agar hum \(f(x) = \tan x\) ke domain ko open interval \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) tak restrict kar dein, to restricted function \(f : \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \to \mathbb{R}\) one-one aur onto ban jata hai, yani invertible. Domain \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) aur range \((-\infty, \infty)\) wale is function ko principal tangent function kehte hain. Inverse tangent function yun defined hai:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "the line \(y = 2\) intersect the graph" chhapa hai; sahi "intersects" hai. Sirf grammar ki ghalti.

blocks.text_alt: y equals tangent inverse of x if and only if x equals tangent of y

blocks.text: \(\tan^{-1} x\) ka domain \((-\infty, \infty)\) hai aur range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) hai. Yani koi bhi real number andar daal sakte hain, aur jawab hamesha \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke darmiyan ka angle hoga, lekin in dono kinaron (end points) ke barabar kabhi nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is dafa interval open (gol brackets) kyun hai? Kyun ke \(\tan\left(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) defined hi nahin, is liye end points shamil nahin ho sakte. Jab \(x\) \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) se zara upar se chal kar \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) se zara neeche tak jata hai, to \(\tan x\) bohat bari negative values se lagataar barh kar bohat bari positive values tak pahunchta hai, aur har real value sirf ek baar leta hai. Yani \(\mathbb{R}\) par one-to-one bhi aur onto bhi.
Is se sine aur cosine ke muqable mein do farq paida hote hain:
1. \(\tan^{-1} x\) har real number \(x\) qabool karta hai (domain \(\mathbb{R}\)). Maslan \(\tan^{-1} 1000\) bhi mojood hai, jab ke \(\sin^{-1} 1000\) mojood nahin.
2. Is ki value kabhi \(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke barabar nahin hoti: range open hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\tan^{-1} 0\) kya hai? (Jawab: \(0\), kyun ke \(\tan 0 = 0\) aur \(0\) range mein hai.)

blocks.caption: Domain aur range ki adla badli (hamara khulasa)

blocks.text: Kitab ke mutabiq function \(\tan : \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \to \mathbb{R}\) ka graph Figure 9.8(a) mein hai, aur \(\tan^{-1} : (-\infty, \infty) \to \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) ka graph Figure 9.8(b) mein hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = tan x only between minus pi over 2 and pi over 2. It rises through the origin, going down towards minus infinity near x = minus pi over 2 and up towards infinity near x = pi over 2; both lines are dashed asymptotes.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.8(a): Graph of y = tan x from −π/2 to π/2 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.alt: Graph of y = inverse tangent of x for all real x. It rises through the origin and flattens out, approaching the dashed horizontal asymptote y = pi over 2 on the right and y = minus pi over 2 on the left without touching them.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.8(b): Graph of y = tan⁻¹ x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Figure 9.8(a) ki vertical asymptotes \(x = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) Figure 9.8(b) mein horizontal asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) ban gayi hain. Wajah wahi: coordinates jagah badalte hain, to khari (vertical) lines leti hui (horizontal) lines ban jati hain.
Figure 9.8(b) parhiye: bari positive \(x\) par \(\tan^{-1} x\) ki value \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke qareeb pahunchti hai (maslan \(\tan^{-1} 1000 \approx 1.5698\), jab ke \(\frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.5708\)), magar kabhi barabar nahin hoti. Bari negative \(x\) par yeh \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke qareeb jati hai. Curve hamesha upar ki taraf ja raha hai: \(\tan^{-1}\) barhne wala function hai.

Kitab batati hai ke \(\tan^{-1} x\) ka graph principal tangent function \(y = \tan x\) ke graph ko line \(y = x\) mein aaine ki tarah ulta kar ke bhi milta hai (Figure 9.9). Yahan bhi \(y = \tan x\) aur \(y = \tan^{-1} x\) ke graphs line \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se ek doosre ka aaina hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "is also obtain by reflecting" chhapa hai; sahi "is also obtained by reflecting" hai. Aur kitab likhti hai "Observe that the graph of \(y = \tan x\) is symmetric about the line \(y = x\)". Akela \(y = \tan x\) ka graph \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se symmetric nahin. Sahi baat: \(y = \tan x\) (principal) aur \(y = \tan^{-1} x\) ke graphs line \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se symmetric hain, yani ek doosre ke aaine. Yeh wahi ghalti hai jo 9.1.1 aur 9.1.2 mein bhi thi.

blocks.alt: The principal tangent curve, between dashed vertical lines x = plus and minus pi over 2, and the inverse tangent curve, between dashed horizontal lines y = plus and minus pi over 2, drawn with the dashed line y = x. Each curve is the mirror image of the other in that line.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.9: y = tan x and y = tan⁻¹ x are mirror images in the line y = x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Kitab aage kehti hai: sine aur cosine ki tarah tangent ka domain bhi laatadaad intervals mein se kisi ek par restrict ho sakta hai, jaise \(\left(-\frac{3\pi}{2}, -\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\), \(\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}\right)\), ya aam shakal mein \(\left(n\pi - \frac{\pi}{2}, n\pi + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\), range \(\mathbb{R}\) ke saath; is se tangent one-to-one ban jata hai. Agar koi interval na bataya jaye to \(\tan^{-1} x\) woh function hai jis ka domain \((-\infty, \infty)\) aur range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Har interval Figure 9.7 ki ek poori shaakh (branch) hai, do parosi asymptotes ke darmiyan. Har shaakh tamam real values ek ek baar leti hai, is liye koi bhi chal sakti thi; lekin standard (principal) intikhab beech wali shaakh \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) hai, yani \(n = 0\). Ghor kijiye ke tangent ke intervals sine jaise hi hain, bas brackets gol hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(\frac{1}{\tan x} = \cot x\) hai. Hamari misaal: \(\tan^{-1} 1 = \frac{\pi}{4}\), jab ke \(\frac{1}{\tan 1} \approx 0.6421\) (yahan 1 radian hai). Pehle ki tarah, \(-1\) inverse function ka naam hai, power nahin.

blocks.caption: Ab tak ke teen inverse functions (hamara khulasa)

blocks.text: Is table ko ghor se dekhiye aur teen sawal khud se poochiye. Pehla: input par koi pabandi hai? \(\sin^{-1}\) aur \(\cos^{-1}\) mein haan (\(-1\) se \(1\) tak), \(\tan^{-1}\) mein nahin. Doosra: jawab kis hisse mein aayega? \(\sin^{-1}\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) ka jawab daayen aadhe hisse mein (pehla ya chautha quadrant), \(\cos^{-1}\) ka jawab upar wale aadhe hisse mein (pehla ya doosra quadrant). Teesra: kinare shamil hain? \(\sin^{-1}\) aur \(\cos^{-1}\) mein haan (square brackets), \(\tan^{-1}\) mein nahin (gol brackets). Jo student yeh teen sawal har dafa pooch leta hai, woh principal value mein kabhi ghalti nahin karta.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Principal value nikalne ka nuskha (Example 1 isi par chalti hai):
1. Expression ko \(y\) ke barabar rakhiye aur inverse hata kar likhiye, jaise \(\cos y = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
2. Sign ko filhaal bhool kar standard values se reference angle dhoondiye.
3. Ab sign aur principal range dekh kar angle ki jagah tay kijiye: negative value ho to \(\sin^{-1}\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) ka jawab negative angle hoga, lekin \(\cos^{-1}\) ka jawab obtuse angle \(\pi - (\text{reference angle})\) hoga.
4. Aakhir mein check kijiye ke angle range ke andar hai.
Yeh chaar qadam imtihan mein likh kar dikhaiye; is se examiner ko pata chalta hai ke aap ne range ka khayal rakha hai.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin^{-1}\), \(\cos^{-1}\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) ke andar numbers \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) aur \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
Maloom karna: har ek ki principal value, yani sirf ek angle.
Tareeqa: har expression ko \(y\) ke barabar rakho aur definition lagao: \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \sin y\) (cos aur tan ke liye bhi isi tarah). Phir woh ek angle chuno jis ki value sahi ho aur jo principal range mein ho: \(\sin^{-1}\) ke liye \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), \(\cos^{-1}\) ke liye \([0, \pi]\), \(\tan^{-1}\) ke liye \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). Yahi do qadam har principal value ke sawal ka nuskha hain.

(i) Qadam 1: sine wali equation banaiye
\[\text{Let } \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = y\]
\[\Rightarrow \sin y = \frac{1}{2}\]
aur \(y\) ko \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hona chahiye.
Kyun: humein woh angle \(y\) chahiye jis ka sine \(\frac{1}{2}\) ho. Definition kehti hai \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) ka matlab \(x = \sin y\) hai, is liye inverse wali shakal ko seedhi sine wali shakal mein badal diya.

(i) Qadam 2: range ke andar angle chuniye
\[\sin y = \frac{1}{2} = \sin\frac{\pi}{6}\]
\[\Rightarrow y = \frac{\pi}{6}\]
Yani \(\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
Kyun: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\) standard value hai, aur \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) ka sine bhi \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai, lekin woh range se bahar hai, is liye woh jawab nahin.

(ii) Qadam 1: cosine wali equation banaiye
\[\text{Let } \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = y\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos y = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
aur \(y\) ko \([0, \pi]\) mein hona chahiye.
Kyun: humein woh angle chahiye jis ka cosine \(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ho; definition se inverse ko cosine ki equation mein badla.

(ii) Qadam 2: range ke andar angle chuniye
Pehle sign ko bhool kar reference angle (bunyaadi angle) dhoondiye: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), to reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) hai. Ab sign dekhiye: cosine negative hai, aur \([0, \pi]\) mein cosine sirf doosre quadrant mein negative hota hai. Is liye
\[y = \pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6}\]
\[\cos\frac{5\pi}{6} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Yani \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \frac{5\pi}{6}\).
Kyun: \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta\), aur \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) range \([0, \pi]\) mein hai.
Dhyan dein: yahan aksar students \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\) ya \(-\frac{5\pi}{6}\) likh dete hain. \(\cos^{-1}\) ka jawab kabhi negative nahin hota.

(iii) Qadam 1: tangent wali equation banaiye
\[\text{Let } \tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = y\]
\[\Rightarrow \tan y = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
aur \(y\) ko \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) mein hona chahiye.
Kyun: definition se \(y = \tan^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \tan y\).

(iii) Qadam 2: range ke andar angle chuniye
\[\tan y = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\]
\[\Rightarrow y = -\frac{\pi}{6}\]
Yani \(\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{6}\).
Kyun: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), aur tangent odd function hai: \(\tan(-\theta) = -\tan\theta\). Value negative hai, is liye \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) mein angle bhi negative hoga (chautha quadrant).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) ka tangent bhi \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) hai, lekin woh range se bahar hai. (ii) aur (iii) dono mein value negative thi, magar jawab alag qism ke aaye: cosine ne obtuse angle diya, tangent ne negative angle. Yahi range ka kamaal hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2},\ \ \frac{\pi}{6} \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
\[\cos\frac{5\pi}{6} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\ \ \frac{5\pi}{6} \in [0, \pi]\]
\[\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
aur \(-\frac{\pi}{6} \in \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). Har jawab ki value bhi sahi hai aur woh apni principal range ke andar bhi hai, to teeno jawab durust hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se misaal, issi tareeqe se:
(a) \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}\): \(\tan y = \sqrt{3}\), aur \(\tan\frac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}\), jo range mein hai. Jawab \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
(b) \(\tan^{-1}(-1)\): reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{4}\), value negative, to angle negative: \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\). (\(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) ka tangent bhi \(-1\) hai, magar range se bahar.)
(c) \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\): reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), value negative, cosine hai, to \(\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\).
Khud sochiye: \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) kya hoga? (Reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), sine hai aur value negative, to jawab \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\).)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\tan^{-1}\) roz marra mein kahan kaam aata hai? Class XI ki analytic geometry yaad kijiye: kisi line ka slope \(m\) us ke inclination (x-axis se jhukao ka angle) \(\theta\) ka tangent hota hai, yani \(m = \tan\theta\). To agar slope maloom ho aur angle chahiye, to \(\theta = \tan^{-1} m\).
Hamari misaal: ek ramp (dhalwan raasta) har 3 meter aage jane par 1 meter upar uthta hai, to slope \(\frac{1}{3}\) hai aur angle \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3} \approx 0.3218\) radian, yani taqreeban \(18.4^\circ\). Agar ramp ka slope \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) ho, to angle bilkul \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\pi}{6} = 30^\circ\).
Isi tarah ek seedhi (ladder) jis ki height aur zameen par faasla maloom ho, us ka angle bhi \(\tan^{-1}\) se nikalta hai. Yahan range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) bhi maani rakhti hai: upar ki taraf jhuki line ka angle positive, neeche ki taraf jhuki line ka angle negative.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Khud sochiye, phir jawab dekhiye:
(a) Kya \(\tan^{-1} x\) kabhi \(2\) ho sakta hai? (Nahin, kyun ke \(2 > \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.5708\), aur range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) hai.)
(b) \(\tan\left(\tan^{-1} 7\right)\) kya hai? (Jawab \(7\). Recall! box ka \(f(f^{-1}(y)) = y\); yeh har real number ke liye sahi hai, kyun ke \(\tan^{-1}\) ka domain \(\mathbb{R}\) hai.)
(c) \(\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\) kya hai? (\(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) range se bahar hai. \(\tan\frac{3\pi}{4} = -1\), aur \(\tan^{-1}(-1) = -\frac{\pi}{4}\). Jawab \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\), na ke \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Principal tangent function: \(\tan : \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \to \mathbb{R}\), jo bijective hai.
2. \(y = \tan^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \tan y\); domain \(\mathbb{R}\), range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) (open).
3. \(\tan^{-1} x\) ke graph ki horizontal asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) hain; yeh principal tangent ke graph ka \(y = x\) mein aaina hai.
4. Principal ranges: \(\sin^{-1}\): \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\); \(\cos^{-1}\): \([0, \pi]\); \(\tan^{-1}\): \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
5. \(\tan^{-1} x\) ka matlab \(\frac{1}{\tan x}\) nahin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \frac{5\pi}{6}\) likhna: yeh \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) se bahar hai; jawab \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\) hai.
2. \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{6}\) ya \(-\frac{5\pi}{6}\) likhna: \(\cos^{-1}\) kabhi negative nahin hota; jawab \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) hai.
3. End points shamil kar lena: \(\tan^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) ka koi hal nahin, kyun ke \(\tan\frac{\pi}{2}\) undefined hai.
4. Yeh samajhna ke \(\tan^{-1} x\) ke liye bhi \(-1 \le x \le 1\) zaroori hai: is ka domain poora \(\mathbb{R}\) hai.
